His mother, Marie Rose ([née](Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Hébert), is a hairdresser and stylist, while his father, Frank Lawrence Ruffalo Jr., worked as a construction painter.[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1)[[2]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-parade-2) He has two sisters, Tanya Marie (died 2023) and Nicole, and a brother, Scott (died 2008).[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) His father is of [Italian](Italians "Italians") descent, from , ,[[3]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-3) and his mother is of [French Canadian](French_Canadians "French Canadians") and Italian ancestry.[[4]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-4)[[5]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-5) Ruffalo attended both [Catholic](Catholic_school "Catholic school") and [progressive](Progressive_education "Progressive education") schools throughout his education. Ruffalo has described himself as having been a "happy kid",[[6]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-6) although he struggled with undiagnosed [dyslexia](Dyslexia "Dyslexia") and [ADHD](Attention_deficit_hyperactivity_disorder_predominantly_inattentive "Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder predominantly inattentive") as a child and a young adult.[[7]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-RollingStone-7) Ruffalo spent his teen years in [Virginia Beach, Virginia](Virginia_Beach%2C_Virginia "Virginia Beach, Virginia"), where his father worked. He competed in wrestling in junior high and high school in Wisconsin and Virginia. Ruffalo graduated from [First Colonial High School](First_Colonial_High_School "First Colonial High School") in Virginia Beach, where he acted for the Patriot Playhouse. He moved with his family to [San Diego](San_Diego "San Diego"), California and later to [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), where he took classes at the [Stella Adler Conservatory](Stella_Adler_Conservatory "Stella Adler Conservatory") and co-founded the Orpheus Theatre Company.[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) With the theater company, he wrote, directed, and starred in a number of plays. He also spent close to a decade working as a [bartender](Bartender "Bartender").[[8]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-8) ## Career ### Acting He made his screen debut in an episode of *[CBS Summer Playhouse](CBS_Summer_Playhouse "CBS Summer Playhouse")* (1989),[[9]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-9) followed by minor film roles, and was part of the original cast of *[This Is Our Youth](This_Is_Our_Youth "This Is Our Youth")* (1996).[[10]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-10) Ruffalo played 'Vinnie Webber', a minor character in Series 1 Episode 9 of *[Due South](Due_South "Due South")*, first broadcast in Canada in 1994.[[11]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-11) Ruffalo had minor roles in films including *[The Dentist](The_Dentist "The Dentist")* (1996), the low-key crime comedy *[Safe Men](Safe_Men "Safe Men")* (1998), and [Ang Lee](Ang_Lee "Ang Lee")'s [Civil War](American_Civil_War "American Civil War") [western](Western_(genre) "Western (genre)") *[Ride with the Devil](Ride_with_the_Devil_(film) "Ride with the Devil (film)")* (1999). Through a chance meeting with writer [Kenneth Lonergan](Kenneth_Lonergan "Kenneth Lonergan"), Ruffalo began collaborating with him and appeared in several of his plays, including the original cast of *[This is Our Youth](This_is_Our_Youth "This is Our Youth")* (1996), which led to Ruffalo's role as [Laura Linney](Laura_Linney "Laura Linney")'s character's brother in Lonergan's [Academy Award](Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")-nominated 2000 film *[You Can Count on Me](You_Can_Count_on_Me "You Can Count on Me")*.[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) He received favorable reviews for his performance in this film, often earning comparisons to the young [Marlon Brando](Marlon_Brando "Marlon Brando"), and won awards from the [Los Angeles Film Critics Association](Los_Angeles_Film_Critics_Association "Los Angeles Film Critics Association") and [Montreal World Film Festival](Montreal_World_Film_Festival "Montreal World Film Festival").[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) His next role was in 2001 in [Rod Lurie](Rod_Lurie "Rod Lurie")'s *[The Last Castle](The_Last_Castle "The Last Castle")* playing a bookie in a military prison alongside [Robert Redford](Robert_Redford "Robert Redford"). It led to other significant roles, including the films ** (2002), [Isabel Coixet](Isabel_Coixet "Isabel Coixet")'s *[My Life Without Me](My_Life_Without_Me "My Life Without Me")*, [John Woo](John_Woo "John Woo")'s ** (2003), [Jane Campion](Jane_Campion "Jane Campion")'s *[In the Cut](In_the_Cut_(film) "In the Cut (film)")* (2003), [Michel Gondry](Michel_Gondry "Michel Gondry")'s *[Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind](Eternal_Sunshine_of_the_Spotless_Mind "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind")* (2004), and *[We Don't Live Here Anymore](We_Don't_Live_Here_Anymore "We Don't Live Here Anymore")* (2004), which is based on two short stories written by [Andre Dubus](Andre_Dubus "Andre Dubus").[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) He appeared opposite [Jamie Foxx](Jamie_Foxx "Jamie Foxx") and [Tom Cruise](Tom_Cruise "Tom Cruise") as a narcotics detective in [Michael Mann](Michael_Mann_(film_director) "Michael Mann (film director)")'s crime thriller *[Collateral](Collateral_(film) "Collateral (film)")* (2004).[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) In the mid-2000s, Ruffalo appeared as a romantic lead in *[View From the Top](View_from_the_Top "View from the Top")* (2002), *[13 Going on 30](13_Going_on_30 "13 Going on 30")* (2004), *[Just Like Heaven](Just_Like_Heaven_(film) "Just Like Heaven (film)")* (2005) and *[Rumor Has It](Rumor_Has_It_(film) "Rumor Has It (film)")* (2005).[[1]](Mark_Ruffalo#cite_note-actors-1) In 2006, Ruffalo starred in [Clifford Odets](Clifford_Odets "Clifford Odets")'s *[Awake and Sing!](Awake_and_Sing! The world's highest-paid actress in 2018 and 2019, she has featured multiple times on the [*Forbes* Celebrity 100](Forbes_Celebrity_100 "Forbes Celebrity 100") list. *[Time](Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* named her one of the [100 most influential people in the world](Time_100 "Time 100") in 2021. [Johansson's films](Scarlett_Johansson_on_screen_and_stage "Scarlett Johansson on screen and stage") have grossed over $14.3 billion worldwide, making her the [highest-grossing box office star of all time](List_of_highest-grossing_actors "List of highest-grossing actors"). She first appeared on stage in an [off-Broadway](Off-Broadway "Off-Broadway") play as a child actor. Johansson made her film debut in the fantasy comedy *[North](North_(1994_film) "North (1994 film)")* (1994) and gained early recognition for her roles in *[Manny & Lo](Manny_%26_Lo "Manny & Lo")* (1996), *[The Horse Whisperer](The_Horse_Whisperer_(film) "The Horse Whisperer (film)")* (1998), and *[Ghost World](Ghost_World_(film) "Ghost World (film)")* (2001). Her shift to adult roles came in 2003 with *[Lost in Translation](Lost_in_Translation_(film) "Lost in Translation (film)")*, and won a [BAFTA Award for Best Actress](BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Leading_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role") for this performance. She continued to gain praise for playing a 17th-century servant in *[Girl with a Pearl Earring](Girl_with_a_Pearl_Earring_(film) "Girl with a Pearl Earring (film)")* (2003), a troubled teenager in *[A Love Song for Bobby Long](A_Love_Song_for_Bobby_Long "A Love Song for Bobby Long")* (2004) and a seductress in *[Match Point](Match_Point "Match Point")* (2005). The latter marked her first collaboration with [Woody Allen](Woody_Allen "Woody Allen"), who later directed her in *[Scoop](Scoop_(2006_film) "Scoop (2006 film)")* (2006) and *[Vicky Cristina Barcelona](Vicky_Cristina_Barcelona "Vicky Cristina Barcelona")* (2008). Johansson's other works of this period include *[The Prestige](The_Prestige_(film) "The Prestige (film)")* (2006) and the albums *[Anywhere I Lay My Head](Anywhere_I_Lay_My_Head "Anywhere I Lay My Head")* (2008) and *[Break Up](Break_Up_(album) "Break Up (album)")* (2009), both of which charted on the [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). In 2010, Johansson debuted on [Broadway](Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in a revival of *[A View from the Bridge](A_View_from_the_Bridge "A View from the Bridge")*, which won her a [Tony Award for Best Featured Actress](Tony_Award_for_Best_Performance_by_a_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Performance by a Featured Actress in a Play"), and began portraying [Black Widow](Natasha_Romanoff_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Natasha Romanoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") film *[Iron Man 2](Iron_Man_2 "Iron Man 2")*. She reprised the role in eight films, leading up to her solo feature [*Black Widow*](Black_Widow_(2021_film) "Black Widow (2021 film)") (2021), gaining global stardom. During this period, Johansson starred in the science fiction films *[Her](Her_(film) "Her (film)")* (2013), *[Under the Skin](Under_the_Skin_(2013_film) "Under the Skin (2013 film)")* (2013) and *[Lucy](Lucy_(2014_film) "Lucy (2014 film)")* (2014). She received two simultaneous [Academy Award](Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations—[Best Actress](Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") and [Best Supporting Actress](Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress")—for the respective roles of an actress going through a divorce in the drama *[Marriage Story](Marriage_Story "Marriage Story")* (2019) and a single mother in [Nazi Germany](Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany") in the satire *[Jojo Rabbit](Jojo_Rabbit "Jojo Rabbit")* (2019), becoming one of [the few actors](List_of_actors_nominated_for_multiple_Academy_Awards_in_the_same_year "List of actors nominated for multiple Academy Awards in the same year") to achieve this feat. Labeled a [sex symbol](Sex_symbol "Sex symbol"), Johansson has been referred to as one of the world's most attractive women by various media outlets. She is a prominent brand endorser and supports several charitable causes. Divorced from actor [Ryan Reynolds](Ryan_Reynolds "Ryan Reynolds") and businessman Romain Dauriac, Johansson has been married to comedian [Colin Jost](Colin_Jost "Colin Jost") since 2020. She has two children, one with Dauriac and another with Jost. ## Early life Scarlett Ingrid Johansson was born on November 22, 1984, in the borough of New York City.[[2]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-2)[[3]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-3)[[4]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-PBS-4) Johansson's father, Karsten Olaf Johansson, is an architect originally from , Denmark. Through him, she is a granddaughter of [Ejner Johansson](Ejner_Johansson "Ejner Johansson"), an art historian, screenwriter, and film director, whose own father was Swedish.[[5]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-tirti-5)[[4]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-PBS-4) Her mother, New Yorker Melanie Sloan, has worked as a producer. She comes from an [Ashkenazi Jewish](Ashkenazi_Jewish "Ashkenazi Jewish") family who fled [Poland](History_of_the_Jews_in_Poland "History of the Jews in Poland") and [Russia](History_of_the_Jews_in_Russia "History of the Jews in Russia"), originally surnamed Schlamberg,[[4]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-PBS-4) and Johansson identifies as Jewish.[[6]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-femau1-6)[[7]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-ashref-7)[[8]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-8) She has an older sister named Vanessa, who is also an actress, an older brother named Adrian, and a twin brother named Hunter.[[9]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-9) Johannson also has an older half-brother named Christian from her father's first marriage, and holds dual American and Danish citizenship.[[10]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-recordd-10)[[11]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-11) On a 2017 episode of 's *[Finding Your Roots](Finding_Your_Roots "Finding Your Roots")*, she discovered that her maternal great-grandfather's brother and extended family died during [the Holocaust](The_Holocaust "The Holocaust") in the [Warsaw Ghetto](Warsaw_Ghetto "Warsaw Ghetto").[[12]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-12) Johansson attended [PS 41](PS_41 "PS 41"), an elementary school in [Greenwich Village](Greenwich_Village "Greenwich Village"), Manhattan.[[13]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-13) Her parents divorced when she was thirteen.[[14]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-BTPB07-14) She was particularly close to her maternal grandmother, Dorothy Sloan, a bookkeeper and schoolteacher. They often spent time together and Johansson considered Dorothy her best friend.[[15]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-15) Interested in a career in the spotlight from an early age, Johansson often put on song-and-dance routines for her family. She was particularly fond of musical theater and [jazz hands](Jazz_hands "Jazz hands").[[16]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-bio-16)[[17]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-localfav-17) Johansson took lessons in [tap dance](Tap_dance "Tap dance"), and states that her parents were supportive of her career choice. She has described her childhood as very ordinary.[[18]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-18) As a child, Johansson practiced acting by staring in the mirror until she made herself cry, wanting to be like [Judy Garland](Judy_Garland "Judy Garland") in *[Meet Me in St. Louis](Meet_Me_in_St._Louis "Meet Me in St. Louis")*. At age seven, she was devastated when a talent agent signed one of her brothers instead of her, but later decided to become an actress anyway. After enrolling at the [Lee Strasberg Theatre Institute](Lee_Strasberg_Theatre_Institute "Lee Strasberg Theatre Institute") and auditioning for commercials, Johansson soon lost interest, stating "I didn't want to promote Wonder Bread."[[19]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-nymag-19) She shifted her focus to film and theater,[[20]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-peoplebio-20) making her first stage appearance with two lines in the [off-Broadway](Off-Broadway "Off-Broadway") play *Sophistry* with [Ethan Hawke](Ethan_Hawke "Ethan Hawke"),[[21]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-21)[[20]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-peoplebio-20) Around this time, Johansson began studying at the [Professional Children's School](Professional_Children's_School "Professional Children's School"), a private educational institution for aspiring child actors in Manhattan.[[16]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-bio-16) ## Acting career See also: [Scarlett Johansson on screen and stage](Scarlett_Johansson_on_screen_and_stage "Scarlett Johansson on screen and stage") and [List of awards and nominations received by Scarlett Johansson](List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Scarlett_Johansson "List of awards and nominations received by Scarlett Johansson") ### 1994–2002: Early work and breakthrough At age nine, Johansson made her film debut as [John Ritter](John_Ritter "John Ritter")'s daughter in the fantasy comedy *[North](North_(1994_film) "North (1994 film)")* (1994).[[20]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-peoplebio-20) She says that when she was on the film set, she knew intuitively what to do.[[19]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-nymag-19) She later played minor roles such as the daughter of [Sean Connery](Sean_Connery "Sean Connery")'s and [Kate Capshaw](Kate_Capshaw "Kate Capshaw")'s characters in the mystery thriller *[Just Cause](Just_Cause_(film) "Just Cause (film)")* (1995), and an art student in *[If Lucy Fell](If_Lucy_Fell "If Lucy Fell")* (1996).[[22]](Scarlett_Johansson#cite_note-Thomson2010-22) Johansson's first leading role was as Amanda, the younger sister of a pregnant teenager who runs away from her [foster home](Foster_care "Foster care") in *[Manny & Lo](Manny_%26_Lo "Manny & Lo")* (1996) alongside [Aleksa Palladino](Aleksa_Palladino "Aleksa Palladino") and her brother, Hunter. Her performance received positive reviews: one written for the *[San Francisco Chronicle](San_Francisco_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")* noted, "[the film] grows on you, largely because of the charm of ... **Jeremy Lee Renner**[[1]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-tvg-1) (born January 7, 1971)[[2]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-2) is an American actor. He began his career by appearing in [independent films](Independent_film "Independent film") such as *[Dahmer](Dahmer_(film) "Dahmer (film)")* (2002) and *[Neo Ned](Neo_Ned "Neo Ned")* (2005), then supporting roles in bigger films, such as *[S.W.A.T.](S.W.A.T._(film) "S.W.A.T. (film)")* (2003) and *[28 Weeks Later](28_Weeks_Later "28 Weeks Later")* (2007). Renner gained [Academy Award](Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations for [Best Actor](Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") for his performance as a soldier in *[The Hurt Locker](The_Hurt_Locker "The Hurt Locker")* (2009) and for [Best Supporting Actor](Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor") for playing a hot-headed robber in *[The Town](The_Town_(2010_film) "The Town (2010 film)")* (2010).

Renner has played [Clint Barton / Hawkeye](Clint_Barton_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Clint Barton (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe"), including in *[The Avengers](The_Avengers_(2012_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")* (2012) and in the [Disney+](Disney%2B "Disney+") miniseries *[Hawkeye](Hawkeye_(miniseries) "Hawkeye (miniseries)")* (2021). He also appeared in the action films *[Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol](Mission%3A_Impossible_%E2%80%93_Ghost_Protocol "Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol")* (2011), *[The Bourne Legacy](The_Bourne_Legacy_(film) "The Bourne Legacy (film)")* (2012), *[Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters](Hansel_%26_Gretel%3A_Witch_Hunters "Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters")* (2013) and *[Mission: Impossible – Rogue Nation](Mission%3A_Impossible_%E2%80%93_Rogue_Nation "Mission: Impossible – Rogue Nation")* (2015); and the dramas *[American Hustle](American_Hustle "American Hustle")* (2013), *[Arrival](Arrival_(film) "Arrival (film)")* (2016), and *[Wind River](Wind_River_(film) "Wind River (film)")* (2017). Since 2021, he has starred in the [Paramount+](Paramount%2B "Paramount+") crime thriller series *[Mayor of Kingstown](Mayor_of_Kingstown "Mayor of Kingstown")*.

## Early life

Renner was born in [Modesto, California](Modesto%2C_California "Modesto, California"), to mother Valerie Cearley ([née](Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Tague) and father Lee Renner, who managed McHenry Bowl, a Modesto bowling alley, in the 1980s.[[3]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-Telegraph-MI-2011-3)[[4]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-ModestoBee-LongRoad-2010-4)[[5]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-Cinefilos-2012-5) His parents married as teenagers and divorced when he was ten.[[6]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-ModestoBee-HugeTree-2008-6)[[7]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-details.com-7)[[8]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-8) He is the oldest of seven siblings, the youngest of whom was born in 2011.[[9]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-9) He is of Irish and German descent.[[10]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-10)

Renner graduated from [Fred C. Beyer High School](Fred_C._Beyer_High_School "Fred C. Beyer High School") in Modesto in 1989.[[4]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-ModestoBee-LongRoad-2010-4) He attended [Modesto Junior College](Modesto_Junior_College "Modesto Junior College"), where he studied computer science and criminology, before he took a drama class as an elective and decided to pursue acting.[[4]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-ModestoBee-LongRoad-2010-4)[[11]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-ref2-11)

## Career

### Early work

Renner made his film debut as an underachieving student in the 1995 comedy *[National Lampoon's Senior Trip](National_Lampoon's_Senior_Trip "National Lampoon's Senior Trip")*.[[12]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-LarryKingNow-KillMessenger-2014-12) Although the film was critically panned, he went on to guest star on two television shows, *[Deadly Games](Deadly_Games_(TV_series) "Deadly Games (TV series)")* and *[Strange Luck](Strange_Luck "Strange Luck")*, and had a minor role in the television film *[A Friend's Betrayal](A_Friend's_Betrayal "A Friend's Betrayal")* as the friend of Paul Hewitt ([Brian Austin Green](Brian_Austin_Green "Brian Austin Green")). Over the next few years, Renner had guest roles in *[Zoe, Duncan, Jack and Jane](Zoe%2C_Duncan%2C_Jack_and_Jane "Zoe, Duncan, Jack and Jane")* (1999), *[The Net](The_Net_(U.S._TV_series) "The Net (U.S. TV series)")* (1999), *[The Time of Your Life](Time_of_Your_Life_(U.S._TV_series) "Time of Your Life (U.S. TV series)")* (1999), and *[Angel](Angel_(1999_TV_series) "Angel (1999 TV series)")* (2000).[[13]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-13) In 2001 Renner had a small role in an episode of *[CSI: Crime Scene Investigation](CSI%3A_Crime_Scene_Investigation "CSI: Crime Scene Investigation")*. Renner worked as a makeup artist during this period to help make ends meet.[[14]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-14)

### Early success: 2002–2008

In 2002, Renner starred in *[Dahmer](Dahmer_(film) "Dahmer (film)")* as the eponymous serial killer [Jeffrey Dahmer](Jeffrey_Dahmer "Jeffrey Dahmer"). He found the non-fiction role a challenge to cope with after he had finished shooting the film, knowing that Dahmer had murdered seventeen victims.[[15]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-15) His performance was well received, and he gained a nomination for the [Independent Spirit Award for Best Lead Male](Independent_Spirit_Award_for_Best_Lead_Male "Independent Spirit Award for Best Lead Male"). He also appeared in [Pink](Pink_(singer) "Pink (singer)")'s 2003 music video for her song "[Trouble](Trouble_(Pink_song) "Trouble (Pink song)")" as a Bad Boy Sheriff.[[16]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-16) Renner went on to appear in *[S.W.A.T.](S.W.A.T._(film) "S.W.A.T. (film)")*[[17]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-17) as the former police partner of [Colin Farrell](Colin_Farrell "Colin Farrell")'s character in 2003 and *[The Heart Is Deceitful Above All Things](The_Heart_Is_Deceitful_Above_All_Things "The Heart Is Deceitful Above All Things")* in 2004.[[18]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-18)

In 2005, Renner starred with [Julia Stiles](Julia_Stiles "Julia Stiles") and [Forest Whitaker](Forest_Whitaker "Forest Whitaker") in *[A Little Trip to Heaven](A_Little_Trip_to_Heaven "A Little Trip to Heaven")*,[[19]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-19) with roles in *[North Country](North_Country_(film) "North Country (film)")* and *[12 and Holding](12_and_Holding "12 and Holding")*. He next starred as a neo-Nazi skinhead who is admitted into a psychiatric hospital in *[Neo Ned](Neo_Ned "Neo Ned")* with [Gabrielle Union](Gabrielle_Union "Gabrielle Union"). The film won awards at multiple film festivals, including the [Palm Beach International Film Festival](Palm_Beach_International_Film_Festival "Palm Beach International Film Festival") Award for Best Actor. Renner also had a small (though uncredited) role in skateboard film *[Lords of Dogtown](Lords_of_Dogtown "Lords of Dogtown")* as the manager of [Emile Hirsch](Emile_Hirsch "Emile Hirsch")'s character. In 2006, he starred with [Ginnifer Goodwin](Ginnifer_Goodwin "Ginnifer Goodwin") in *Love Comes to the Executioner*.

In 2007 Renner had supporting roles in the critically acclaimed *[The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford](The_Assassination_of_Jesse_James_by_the_Coward_Robert_Ford "The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford")* as [Wood Hite](Wood_Hite "Wood Hite"), the cousin of outlaw [Jesse James](Jesse_James "Jesse James") (portrayed by [Brad Pitt](Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt")), and as Sergeant Doyle in *[28 Weeks Later](28_Weeks_Later "28 Weeks Later")*.[[20]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-20) He starred with [Minnie Driver](Minnie_Driver "Minnie Driver") in *[Take](Take_(film) "Take (film)")* and guest-starred as a patient (a reckless rock musician) in an episode of *[House](House_(TV_series) "House (TV series)")*. Renner had a role in the pilot of *[The Oaks](The_Oaks_(TV_series) "The Oaks (TV series)")*,[[21]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-21) but the series was not picked up.[[22]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-22)

### 2009–2012: critical and commercial breakout

After starring with [Dallas Roberts](Dallas_Roberts "Dallas Roberts") in the comedy-drama *Ingenious* and starring in the short-lived television series *[The Unusuals](The_Unusuals "The Unusuals")*, Renner portrayed U.S. Army bomb disposal expert Sergeant First Class William James in the 2009 Iraq war thriller *[The Hurt Locker](The_Hurt_Locker "The Hurt Locker")* (directed by [Kathryn Bigelow](Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow")). The role earned him several awards in the Best Actor category and his first Academy Award nomination for [Best Actor](Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor")[[23]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-23) as well a [Screen Actors Guild Award](Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award") nomination.[[24]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-24)

In 2010, Renner's performance in [Ben Affleck](Ben_Affleck "Ben Affleck")'s *[The Town](The_Town_(2010_film) "The Town (2010 film)")* alongside [Jon Hamm](Jon_Hamm "Jon Hamm"), [Blake Lively](Blake_Lively "Blake Lively"), [Slaine](Slaine_(rapper) "Slaine (rapper)") and [Michael Yebba](Michael_Yebba "Michael Yebba") received extremely positive reviews and earned Renner's second Academy Award nomination, for [Best Supporting Actor](Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[25]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-25) He also gained his first Golden Globe nomination for [Best Supporting Actor](Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture")[[26]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-26) and his second Screen Actors Guild nomination.[[27]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-27) *[The Hollywood Reporter](The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* named Renner as one of the young male actors who are "pushing – or being pushed" into taking over Hollywood as the new "A-List".[[28]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-28)

In 2011, Renner had an uncredited cameo appearance as [Hawkeye](Hawkeye_(Clint_Barton) "Hawkeye (Clint Barton)") in *[Thor](Thor_(film) "Thor (film)")* for familiarity with his character for *[The Avengers](The_Avengers_(2012_film) "The Avengers (2012 film)")*, which was released in May 2012.[[29]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-29)[[30]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-30)[[31]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-31) The same year, he also starred in the fourth film in the [*Bourne* franchise](Bourne_(film_series) "Bourne (film series)"), *[The Bourne Legacy](The_Bourne_Legacy_(film) "The Bourne Legacy (film)")*, which was written and directed by [Tony Gilroy](Tony_Gilroy "Tony Gilroy").[[32]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-32) Renner played a new lead character, Aaron Cross, in place of [Jason Bourne](Jason_Bourne "Jason Bourne"), who was played by [Matt Damon](Matt_Damon "Matt Damon") in the first three films. Renner has expressed interest in doing a *Bourne* film with Damon in the future, stating that "[it] would be kick-ass. I love Matt".[[33]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-33)

### 2013–present: continued work

Renner starred in the action horror film *[Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters](Hansel_%26_Gretel%3A_Witch_Hunters "Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters")* (released in January 2013), in which he and [Gemma Arterton](Gemma_Arterton "Gemma Arterton") played Hansel and Gretel, respectively. The 3-D film was set 15 years after [Hansel and Gretel](Hansel_and_Gretel "Hansel and Gretel") killed the witch who kidnapped them.[[34]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-34) Renner was also featured in the ensemble cast of [David O. Russell](David_O._Russell "David O. Russell")'s dramedy *[American Hustle](American_Hustle "American Hustle")*, based on the controversial [FBI](Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") [ABSCAM](Abscam "Abscam") operation of the late 1970s and early 1980s. The film, which was released in December 2013, also starred [Christian Bale](Christian_Bale "Christian Bale"), [Bradley Cooper](Bradley_Cooper "Bradley Cooper"), [Amy Adams](Amy_Adams "Amy Adams") and [Jennifer Lawrence](Jennifer_Lawrence "Jennifer Lawrence") in principal roles. The film earned much critical acclaim, including the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture](Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Cast_in_a_Motion_Picture "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture") and a nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Picture](Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). In October 2014, Renner starred as journalist [Gary Webb](Gary_Webb "Gary Webb") in the [Focus Features](Focus_Features "Focus Features") film [*Kill the Messenger*](Kill_the_Messenger_(2014_film) "Kill the Messenger (2014 film)"), based on Webb's book [*Dark Alliance*](Dark_Alliance_(book) "Dark Alliance (book)"). Renner also co-produced the film. In December 2014, [Crackle](Crackle_(company) "Crackle (company)") aired *The Throwaways*, a film for which Renner served as executive producer.[[35]](Jeremy_Renner#cite_note-35)
